limitations_admitted.value: L_IR conversion relies on one point of the IR SED and dust SED templates

evidence.quote: the conversion from the 160 μm flux to $L_{IR}$ in this work is based only on one point in the infrared SED

referee_caveats_inferred: Conclusions quote mass-proxy totals as -1.07 and -1.48 but Table 2 gives GSMF z~5.5 = -1.50 and UVLF z~4.5 = -1.48, so the text and table mix up proxies
Bin edges, membership and per-bin fluxes are not tabulated, so stacks cannot be rebuilt from the text
Mass-proxy results rely on SED-fit masses and extrapolation over about 6 dex in mass
Main-sequence slope at z~5.5 rests on three points and has large uncertainty
L_IR from a single 160 um flux point; T_dust and template choice dominate systematics

missing_for_reproduction: ALMA project code(s), CASA/pipeline versions and tclean parameters (deferred to Bethermin+20)
Per-bin stellar mass, M_FUV and stacked flux tables
emcee priors, likelihood and chain settings

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Not stated; 118 targets, so roughly tens to hundreds of GB of visibilities, or a few GB if starting from released continuum images
reproducibility.score_reason: Final numbers and methods are given, but bin definitions, project code, imaging parameters and fit settings are deferred or missing, and stacking code is not stated as public
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Paper prints no project code or public-data statement and omits the bin definitions and fit settings needed to redo the stacks; results are numeric but recipe is incomplete
